text:
Predicates:
Twins(x) ::: x is a twin.
Triplets(x) ::: x is a triplet.
Siblings(x, y) ::: x has siblings y.
SameAge(x, y) ::: x and y are the same age.
HangOutWith(x, y) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with y.
PlayWith(x, y) ::: x spends a lot of time playing with y.
ComplainAbout(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
DevelopBonds(x, y) ::: x develops strong bonds with y.

Premises:
∀x (Twins(x) ∨ Triplets(x) → (HangOutWith(x, Siblings(x)) ∧ PlayWith(x, Siblings(x)))) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
∀x (SameAge(Siblings(x), y) → (Twins(x) ∨ Triplets(x))) ::: If people have siblings who are the same age, then they are twins or triplets.
∀x (ComplainAbout(x) → SameAge(Siblings(x), y)) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who are the same age.
∀x (¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) → ¬DevelopBonds(x, FamilyMembers(x))) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds with their family members.
∀x ((HangOutWith(x, Siblings(x)) ∧ PlayWith(x, Siblings(x))) → ¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings, then they often did not live at home regularly.
(Twins(luke) ∨ Triplets(luke) ∧ DevelopBonds(luke, FamilyMembers(luke))) ⊕ ¬(Twins(luke) ∨ Triplets(luke) ∨ DevelopBonds(luke, FamilyMembers(luke))) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds with his family members, or he neither is a twin or triplet nor develops strong bonds with his family members.

Conclusion:
ComplainAbout(luke) ::: Luke complains often about annoying siblings.
